newsitem.title: USA: Colombia $1.0 global well oversubscribed - syndicate.
newsitem.headline: Colombia $1.0 global well oversubscribed - syndicate.

text.p: Colombia's $1.0 global bond issue was well-oversubscribed by investors worldwide with demand of nearly $4.0 billion, said a syndicate manager at Merrill Lynch & Co, which co-lead the bond offering with J.P. Morgan Securities.
"The total book was almost $4.0 billion. It was around $3.6 to $3.7 billion," said Dan Vallimarescu, a director in the capital markets group at Merrill Lynch & Co in New York.
He said the size of the deal, which was originally $750 million, was increased after demand grew to about $2.6 billion for the 10-year tranche.

"We started out with $750 million 10-year and had an order book of around $2.6 billion for that and when we saw that the demand was really so strong the Republic (of Colombia) agreed to increase it by $250 million with the 30-yr tranche," said Vallimarescu, who also pointed out that demand for the 30-year tranche was in excess of $1.0 billion.

Vallimarescu said the global bond offering was clearly a huge success because of the oversubscribtion and the very tight spread. But he also attributed the success to the global distribution in the United States, Europe and in Asia.
He said book orders on the $750 million 10-year tranche totalled about 210 accounts and orders for the 30-year comprised of roughly 90 accounts.
"There is some duplication among those two but there are also people that are in the 30 but are not in the 10," Vallimarescu said.
John Massad, head of debt syndicate at J.P. Morgan Securities, noted that there was very good demand from Korea.

Massad said the demand from Korea was anticipated and that was why the the roadshow stopped off in Seoul. "I would say that the degree to which they participate is clearly growing. I think they see Colombia as a real opportunity from a credit standpoint."
Vallimarescu also noted that the quality of the orders were not only significant for Colombia but for the emerging markets overall.

"These are people in large part who are not traditional emerging market investors. These are mainstream blue chip invesment-grade buyers of debt who are very comfortable with the Colombian risk," he said.

"No one debates that we pushed the pricing very aggressively on this bond but there is the real opportunity for price performance over time as we see the credit improve as many people expect," added Massad.
